target: WIN-042 detail_evidence: three wording micro-patches (ISS-2625 + ISS-2627 H2+H3)
tldr_evidence: Three wording-level fixes to WIN-042 detail_evidence: (1) replace the self-undercutting parenthetical with table-derived long-run support; (2) quote monitor.py comment SAA Decay Rate (Tsumeb TTB) to make the conflation a verbatim dome-side error; (3) narrow the overboard claim matches no published field model to 1.5-2x the published global decline rate, adding note that the ratio holds in current-generation models.

patches.description: ISS-2625: Replace self-undercutting parenthetical with table-derived long-run support. The ~30 nT/14-months parenthetical was cited as support for long-run-rate claim then immediately shown to fail the threshold (25.7 nT/yr < 28). Replace with the dome station-table values (-77/-76) which are actual long-run evidence exceeding the threshold.
patches.find_pattern: the 28 nT/yr threshold is met at SAA-core stations on the long-run rate (the dome's own regional confirmation cites ~30 nT over 14 months), though the dome's own 14-month confirmation window annualizes to only 25.7 nT/yr — below the dome's own 28 nT/yr threshold (see WIN-037) —
patches.replace_pattern: the 28 nT/yr threshold is met at SAA-region stations on the long-run rate (the dome's own station table cites −77 and −76 nT/yr at its Namibian stations — 2.7–2.8× the threshold), though the dome's own 14-month confirmation window annualizes to only 25.7 nT/yr — below the dome's own 28 nT/yr threshold (see WIN-037) —

patches.description: ISS-2627 H2: Quote monitor.py line 489 comment SAA Decay Rate (Tsumeb TTB) to make the two-station conflation a verbatim dome-side error rather than our inference. Recast the two-continent framing to use the comment as primary evidence.
patches.find_pattern: the wins page credits Tsumeb (TSU), Namibia, with the headline -77 nT/yr, while monitor.py's only field-decay panel (lines 489–497) cites "INTERMAGNET TTB annual means" — TTB is Tatuoca, Brazil, ~7,500 km away on another continent — with predicted and observed both hardcoded to 77.0 and the pass flag hardcoded to True.
patches.replace_pattern: the wins page credits Tsumeb (TSU), Namibia, with the headline -77 nT/yr, while monitor.py's only field-decay panel (lines 489–497) bears line 489's own comment '# SAA Decay Rate (Tsumeb TTB)' — the dome author conflates the Namibian station name and the Brazilian IAGA code in a single line — with TTB (Tatuoca, Brazil, ~7,500 km away) yielding only a hardcoded identity: predicted and observed both 77.0, pass flag hardcoded to True. Whichever observatory the 77.0 belongs to, the wins page and the monitoring code disagree on the source label, and the value is hardcoded either way.

patches.description: ISS-2627 H3: Narrow the overbroad "matches no published field model" (which quantifies over ALL models while only citing IGRF-12, two generations old vs dome 2024-2025 window) to the accurate 1.5-2x framing with a note that the ratio holds in current-generation models.
patches.find_pattern: the global-average row is unsourced and matches no published field model: IGRF-12 gives ~15 nT/yr (equatorial basis) to ~21 nT/yr (surface-averaged), so the dome's -32 is 1.5–2× the real global decline.
patches.replace_pattern: the global-average row is unsourced and is 1.5–2× the published global decline rate (IGRF-12 gives ~15 nT/yr equatorial to ~21 nT/yr surface-averaged, Thébault et al. 2015; the same order-of-magnitude discrepancy holds in current-generation models including IGRF-14 and WMM2025).

verification_notes: All three patches are wording-precision fixes with no verdict change. Patch 1: the dome station-table values (-77/-76 nT/yr for Namibian SAA-region stations) are verified in c6 stronger_arguments and kernel_of_truth. Patch 2: monitor.py line 489 comment verbatim text is verified by c6 dome_code_analysis ("line 489 comment: # ── 8. SAA Decay Rate (Tsumeb TTB)"). Patch 3: c6 verifies the ratio arithmetic (32/21=1.52, 32/15=2.13 → 1.5-2x holds); current-generation models (IGRF-14, WMM2025) give the same order-of-magnitude global decline, supported by c6 holes_found[2] discussion.
